name: Apricot
water: Deep and infrequent — let the soil dry between soakings
likes: A sheltered spot — its early blooms are frost-prone
care: Prune in dry weather after fruiting; thin young fruit so limbs don't break
recipe: Halve and roast with honey until jammy — or just eat them warm off the tree.

name: Peach
water: A deep weekly soak, more while fruiting
likes: Heat and good airflow
care: Thin fruit to a hand-width apart; prune to an open vase shape each winter
recipe: Grill cut-side down until caramelized, then serve with yogurt and mint.

name: Fig
water: Keep the pot evenly moist, never soggy
likes: Warm roots and a pot it can travel in
care: Overwinter it somewhere above freezing; prune lightly as it wakes in spring
recipe: Quarter and drape with prosciutto, or roast with honey and a knob of goat cheese.

name: Cherry
water: Even moisture, a deep soak weekly
likes: Cold winters — it's a hardy bush cherry
care: Keep a second variety close for pollination; net it against birds at fruiting
recipe: Pit and simmer into a quick 10-minute compote for yogurt or pancakes.

name: Cherry
water: Even moisture, a deep soak weekly
likes: Cold winters — it's a hardy bush cherry
care: Planted to pollinate the Romeo bush; net both against birds at fruiting
recipe: Pit and simmer into a quick 10-minute compote for yogurt or pancakes.

name: Cherry
water: Even moisture, a deep soak weekly
likes: Cold winters — it's a hardy bush cherry
care: Keep a second variety close for pollination; net it against birds at fruiting
recipe: Pit and simmer into a quick 10-minute compote for yogurt or pancakes.

name: Pawpaw
light: Part shade young, full sun once established
water: Consistently moist — never let it dry out
likes: A second tree nearby for cross-pollination
care: Shade the trunk its first year; be patient — fruit takes a few seasons
recipe: Scoop the custard flesh raw, or blend into ice cream — it tastes like banana-mango.

name: Serviceberry
water: Moderate and even
soil: Adaptable as long as it drains
likes: A spot where you can beat the birds to the berries
care: Barely needs pruning; pick the berries in early summer
recipe: Use it like a blueberry — pancakes, jam, or straight off the branch.

name: Blueberry
water: Steady moisture — the shallow roots dry out fast
likes: Acidic soil and a deep mulch of pine or bark
care: Mulch deep; strip the first year's fruit so it builds roots
recipe: Pancakes, or simmer into a quick compote with a squeeze of lemon.

recipe: Pancakes, or simmer into a quick compote with a squeeze of lemon.

name: Raspberry
water: An inch or two a week
likes: Room to spread and a wire to lean on
care: Cut spent canes to the ground after fruiting; thin the new ones
recipe: Mash with a little sugar over yogurt, or fold straight into muffin batter.

name: Honeyberry
water: Even moisture
likes: A different honeyberry variety nearby to pollinate
care: Almost no pruning needed; it ripens first, so net early against birds
recipe: Tart enough to shine in jam, or blend into smoothies like a blueberry.

name: Honeyberry
water: Even moisture
likes: A different honeyberry variety nearby to pollinate
care: Almost no pruning needed; it ripens first, so net early against birds
recipe: Tart enough to shine in jam, or blend into smoothies like a blueberry.

name: Kiwi
water: Deep and regular
likes: A strong trellis and a male vine nearby
care: Train one main trunk up the arch; prune hard in winter
recipe: Slice over a pavlova, or blend into a bright green smoothie.

name: Grape
water: Deep but infrequent once established
likes: Airflow and a sturdy trellis
care: Prune hard every winter — most of last year's growth comes off
recipe: Roast on the vine until blistered for a cheese board, or freeze for snacks.

name: Rhubarb
water: Consistent moisture
likes: A shovelful of compost each spring
care: Don't harvest the first year; pull stalks, never cut — and never eat the leaves
recipe: Stew with strawberries and sugar into a classic compote or crumble.

name: Asparagus
note: The long game — first real harvest takes a couple years
water: Deep and regular through the season
likes: A permanent bed it will never be dug up in
care: No harvest for two years; let the ferns grow to feed the crowns
recipe: Roast with olive oil and lemon — 8 minutes at 425°F, no more.

name: Lavender
water: Low — drought-tolerant once established
likes: Dry feet and poor soil
care: Shear lightly after it blooms; never let it sit wet
recipe: Steep the buds into a simple syrup for lemonade and cocktails.

name: Coneflower
water: Low once established
likes: Being left alone — the pollinators handle the rest
care: Deadhead for more blooms, or leave the seed heads for the birds
recipe: Dry the petals and root for a homegrown echinacea tea.

name: Arugula
water: Even moisture
likes: Cool weather — it bolts the moment it's hot
care: Cut the outer leaves young; sow a fresh patch every couple of weeks
recipe: Toss raw with lemon, good olive oil, and shaved parmesan.

name: Broccoli
water: Consistent — about an inch a week
likes: Cool weather and steady feeding
care: Cut the central head before it flowers; side shoots keep coming
recipe: Roast hard at 450°F until the edges char, then finish with garlic.

name: Mustard
water: Even moisture
likes: Cool weather
care: Pick leaves young and mild — the flavor sharpens as it heats up
recipe: Quick-braise the greens with garlic and a splash of vinegar.

name: Onion
water: Even moisture while bulbing
likes: Long summer days to size up
care: Stop watering when the tops flop; cure the bulbs somewhere dry and airy
recipe: Slow-caramelize for 40 patient minutes — the base of everything.

name: Beet
water: Steady — uneven water turns them woody
likes: Being thinned — each 'seed' is really a cluster
care: Thin to a few inches apart; eat the greens too
recipe: Roast whole in foil, then peel, slice, and dress with goat cheese.

name: Cauliflower
water: Consistent — stress ruins the head
likes: Cool, even conditions
care: Tie the leaves up over the head to keep it white
recipe: Roast it whole, basted in spiced butter, until deep golden.

name: Kale
water: Even moisture
likes: Frost — it actually sweetens
care: Pick from the bottom up and it produces for months
recipe: Massage raw with lemon and oil for salad, or crisp it into chips.

name: Peas
water: Even moisture, more once flowering
likes: Cool weather and something to climb
care: Trellis them early; pick often to keep the pods coming
recipe: Eat raw from the pod, or blanch 60 seconds with mint and butter.

name: Tomato
light: Full sun — eight hours or more
water: Deep and even — irregular water cracks the fruit
likes: Warmth, deep planting, and steady moisture
care: Cage or stake it, pinch the suckers, feed once fruit sets
recipe: Slow-roast with garlic and basil — or just salt and good olive oil.

likes: Warmth, deep planting, and steady moisture

water: Deep and even — irregular water cracks the fruit
likes: Warmth, deep planting, and steady moisture
care: Cage or stake it heavily, pinch the suckers, feed once fruit sets
recipe: Slow-roast with garlic and basil — or just salt and good olive oil.

likes: Warmth, deep planting, and steady moisture
care: Cage or stake it, pinch the suckers, feed once fruit sets
recipe: Slow-roast with garlic and basil — or just salt and good olive oil.

name: Pepper
water: Even moisture, never soggy
likes: Heat — it sulks until the nights warm up
care: Stake heavy plants; harvest often to keep it setting fruit
recipe: Blister whole in a screaming-hot pan, finish with flaky salt — one in ten bites back.

name: Pepper
water: Even moisture, never soggy
likes: Heat — it sulks until the nights warm up
care: Stake heavy plants; harvest often to keep it setting fruit
recipe: Stuff with cheese and roast, or quick-pickle in vinegar, salt, and sugar.

name: Pepper
water: Even moisture, never soggy
likes: Heat — it sulks until the nights warm up
care: Stake heavy plants; harvest often to keep it setting fruit
recipe: Roast until the skin blackens, then peel for silky strips in pasta and salad.

name: Eggplant
water: Even and deep — don't let it wilt
likes: Heat, and then more heat
care: Stake the plant; cut fruit with shears while the skin is glossy
recipe: Char whole over a flame for baba ganoush, or roast in rounds with a miso glaze.

name: Eggplant
water: Even and deep — don't let it wilt
likes: Heat, and then more heat
care: Stake the plant; cut fruit with shears while the skin is glossy
recipe: Char whole over a flame for baba ganoush, or roast in rounds with a miso glaze.

recipe: Char whole over a flame for baba ganoush, or roast in rounds with a miso glaze.

name: Squash
water: Deep, at the base — keep the leaves dry
likes: Room to sprawl and steady water
care: Pick young and often; watch the leaves for borers and mildew
recipe: Slice thin and sauté hot with garlic, or grate into crispy fritters.

name: Squash

likes: Room to sprawl and steady water
care: Pick young and often; watch the leaves for borers and mildew

care: Pick young and often; watch the leaves for borers and mildew
recipe: Slice thin and sauté hot with garlic, or grate into crispy fritters.

name: Corn
water: An inch a week, critical at tasseling
likes: Being planted in a block so it pollinates
care: Hill soil up around the stalks — it anchors the 3 Sisters
recipe: Grill in the husk, then slather with butter, lime, and chili.

name: Pumpkin
water: Deep and even — a lot of it
likes: Space, warmth, and heavy feeding
care: Give the vines room to run; let several small fruit set
recipe: Roast and scoop, or hollow the little ones into edible bowls.

name: Pumpkin
water: Deep and even — a lot of it
likes: Space, warmth, and heavy feeding
care: Give the vines room; keep just one fruit per vine to size it up
recipe: Grown for the scale, not the plate — but always roast the seeds.

name: Butternut Squash
water: Deep and even
likes: A long, warm season to ripen
care: Cure it 10+ days after harvest and it keeps for months
recipe: Cube and roast with sage and brown butter, or blend into a silky soup.

name: Pole Beans
water: Even moisture at flowering and podding
soil: Average — they fix their own nitrogen
likes: Something tall to climb
care: Let them run up the corn; pick often so they keep producing
recipe: Blanch and shock, then toss with butter and toasted almonds.

name: Basil
water: Even moisture
likes: Warmth — anything under 50°F sets it back
care: Pinch the flower buds to keep leaves coming; replant this one after the freeze
recipe: Blend into pesto with pine nuts, garlic, and parmesan.

name: Oregano
water: Low once established
likes: Dry, poor soil
care: Trim it often — the flavor peaks just before it flowers
recipe: Dry it — unbeatable on pizza, tomato sauce, and roast lamb.

name: Thyme
water: Low — it's drought-tolerant
likes: Dry feet and full sun
care: Shear lightly after flowering to keep it from going woody
recipe: Tuck whole sprigs into roasting pans; strip the leaves for soups.

name: Rosemary
water: Low — let it dry between waterings
likes: Warmth and dry roots
care: Bring the pot indoors before a hard frost; prune to shape
recipe: Skewer meat on the woody stems, or infuse it into olive oil.

name: Garlic
water: Even moisture, stop a few weeks before harvest
likes: A cold spell to split into cloves
care: Snap off the scapes; harvest when the lower leaves brown
recipe: Roast a whole head until jammy and spreadable on anything.

name: Nasturtium
water: Moderate
soil: Poor and lean — rich soil gives all leaves, no flowers
likes: Being ignored, honestly
care: Let it trail or mound; eat the peppery flowers and leaves
recipe: Toss the peppery leaves and flowers straight into a salad.

name: Calendula
water: Moderate
likes: Cool weather — it self-sows freely
care: Deadhead for more blooms; the petals are edible
recipe: Scatter the petals into salads, or infuse them into a skin-soothing oil.

name: Zinnia
water: At the base — keep the foliage dry
likes: Heat, and being cut
care: Cut flowers often — the more you take, the more it blooms
recipe: A cut-flower, not a crop — the longest-lasting bouquet in the garden.

name: Marigold
water: Moderate
likes: Hot spots — and it helps deter pests
care: Deadhead spent blooms; tuck it in near tomatoes and squash
recipe: More companion plant than food, but the petals can color rice or butter.

name: Marigold
water: Moderate
likes: Hot spots — and it helps deter pests
care: Deadhead spent blooms; tuck it in near tomatoes and squash
recipe: More companion plant than food, but the petals can color rice or butter.

name: Salvia
water: Low to moderate
likes: Heat — hummingbirds and bees love it
care: Cut back spent spikes for a second flush
recipe: Ornamental here — leave it standing for the hummingbirds and bees.

name: Eucalyptus
water: Moderate
likes: Warmth and full sun
care: Grown as an annual here; cut stems to dry for fragrant foliage
recipe: Hang the stems to dry, then tuck a bunch into the shower for the scent.
